text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests that measure your blood sugar levels.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests that measure your blood sugar levels

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors use three main laboratory tests to diagnose type 2 diabetes:

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar over the past two to three months. A result of 6.5% or higher indicates diabetes.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures blood sugar after you do not eat or drink anything except water for at least eight hours. A result of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.

Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures blood sugar two hours after you drink a special sugary liquid containing 75 grams of glucose. A result of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.

Random Plasma Glucose Test: Used when you have classic symptoms of high blood sugar (such as extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss). A result of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher at any time of day confirms diabetes.

text_blocks.snippet: Except in cases of clear, symptomatic high blood sugar, doctors usually confirm a positive test result by repeating the same test or running a different test on a separate day. You can read more about these standards through the American Diabetes Association.
